text:
Fukuoka's ramen has a noodle-firmness scale with seven levels, from almost raw to very soft. Which would you order? Most first-timers just say "normal" and miss the fun 👇

🎯 Pick your level, then see what locals order 👉 https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-food-beyond-tonkotsu-ramen

🍜 THE SCALE (hardest to softest)

Nama · Harigane · Barikata · Kata · Futsu (normal) · Yawa · Bariyawa

Locals tend to go a little firm. The noodles are very thin and soften fast in the hot soup.

🔁 THE REFILL

When the noodles are gone, keep the soup and order kaedama, a second serving of noodles. It started with Nagahama ramen, for exactly that reason: thin noodles go soft quickly, so you order more instead of a bigger bowl.

💡 THE SMART TIP

Order the kaedama one step softer than your first bowl. By then the soup has cooled, so the noodles soften less.

🌅 THE EARLY ONE

Ganso Nagahamaya started in 1952 as a stall feeding fish-market workers, and it still opens at 6:00. Buy a ticket at the machine and tell the staff your firmness.

🌙 THE LATE ONE

Hakata Ramen Shin-Shin in Tenjin stays open until 3:00.

And when you've had your ramen, Fukuoka has five more dishes eaten in its own way, from soft udon to raw mackerel.
